findings.title: Imported feed/remote HTML is stored and rendered without sanitization (stored XSS)
findings.body: Imported posts use `cook_method: raw_html`, so `Post#cook` returns `raw` as-is and skips the sanitizing pipeline. The HTML comes from RSS item content, which is completely unfiltered, or from a Readability extraction that still allows `href`/`src` with any scheme (e.g. `javascript:`). It is then rendered verbatim on the forum and through `raw post.cooked` in the embed view. Anyone who controls or compromises the feed, or the embedded site's pages, can inject script into the forum origin.

findings.title: Embed URL interpolated unescaped into HTML attribute
findings.body: `"#{url}"` inserts the URL without HTML-escaping. Because the post uses `raw_html`, this markup is never sanitized. The URL can come from the `embed_url` request parameter via `TopicRetriever`, which only checks the host. A path containing `'` or `<` (e.g. `http://host/x'onmouseover=alert(1)`) therefore breaks out of the attribute and injects script. The URL should be escaped with `ERB::Util.html_escape`.

findings.title: `contents <<` mutates the caller's string
findings.body: `contents << ...` appends the 'imported from' footer to the string passed in by the caller. That string may be frozen (raises an error) or reused by the caller, who then silently gets the footer appended. Build a new string with `contents + ...` instead.

findings.title: Protocol-relative URLs are rewritten incorrectly
findings.body: Any `href`/`src` starting with `/` is treated as site-relative, which includes protocol-relative URLs like `//cdn.example.com/img.png`. These are rewritten to `http://host/cdn.example.com/img.png`, breaking external images and links. Values starting with `//` should be excluded.

findings.title: `<%- end if %>` turns the next output statement into the if-condition
findings.body: `end if` followed by a newline makes Ruby take the next generated statement (the logo `link_to` append) as the modifier condition. The logo is appended before the whole if/else block is evaluated, so the header renders in the wrong order, and the block is gated on that append's return value. This should be a plain `<%- end %>`.

findings.title: Crash on feed items without content
findings.body: `i.content.scrub` assumes every item has `content`. Many RSS feeds only provide `description`, so `content` is nil and the call raises NoMethodError. Because the exception is not handled per item, the whole poll aborts. `String#scrub` also requires Ruby 2.1+. Fall back to `i.description` and guard against nil.

findings.title: Kernel#open on a configurable URL allows command execution
findings.body: `open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url)` uses Kernel#open. A value starting with `|` executes a shell command and a plain path reads local files. Use `URI.parse(url).open` or an HTTP client restricted to http(s).

findings.title: Weak postMessage origin check
findings.body: `discourseUrl.indexOf(e.origin) === -1` accepts any origin that is a substring of `discourseUrl`. For example, `https://forum.example` passes when `discourseUrl` is `https://forum.example.com/`. Compare the exact origin parsed from `discourseUrl` instead.

findings.title: Referer used as JS targetOrigin is HTML-escaped, not JS-escaped
findings.body: `'<%= request.referer %>'` inside a `<script>` tag is HTML-escaped, so `&` becomes `&` and the targetOrigin string is corrupted. Embedding request-derived data in JS should use `j`/`to_json`, and should pass only the origin rather than the full referer URL.

findings.title: Public caching of embed responses including the 'loading' page
findings.body: `discourse_expires_in 1.minute` is applied even when the 'loading' template is rendered, so caches can keep serving the loading page after the topic is created. The response also depends on `current_user` and on the referer check, so a shared cache could serve it to other clients and bypass the referer validation.

findings.title: Editing an existing migration to add `force: true`
findings.body: This modifies an already-published migration. It has no effect on databases that already ran it. Where it does run, `force: true` silently drops any existing `top_topics` table. Changes should go in a new migration.
